description: Parameters of the relief layer (experiment E08). Elevations in metres above sea level. 'peak_m' is the highest summit of the Earth analogue; the mean elevation of a 10 km cell on the crest of a range is crest_factor x peak_m above the surrounding plain.

1.note: shields: Canadian, Baltic, African shields 300-600 m

2.note: platforms: Russian and Great Plains platforms 100-400 m

8.note: sedimentary and endorheic basins: West Siberian Plain, Caspian lowland, 0-200 m

3.analogue: worn Palaeozoic belts (Appalachians, Mount Mitchell 2037 m; Urals, Narodnaya 1894 m) after further wear

6.analogue: low rift shoulders away from the canon ranges

margin_ranges.boundary: West Southern trench (Sunset under the southern continent)

8.analogue: Sarawat-Asir, Red Sea rift shoulder on an old belt (Jabal Sawda ~3000 m; officially 3015 m, surveyed 2999 m in 2018)

18.analogue: Etna, arc-related volcano (3326 m; quoted 3326-3357 m, the summit changes with eruptions)

23.analogue: canyon cut into a plateau (Grand Canyon up to ~1800 m deep)

28.analogue: canyon cut into a plateau (Grand Canyon up to ~1800 m deep)

sediment.calibration: fitted (E08 run o, against E07 run g) so that, as in GlobSed (Straume et al. 2019): the 12.9 % of the ocean nearest land holds 3044 m on average, ocean floor more than 200 km beyond that zone 404 m, and the oceans 337 million km3 in all
sediment.note: isostatic surface rise = thickness x (mantle - sediment) / (mantle - water)

residual_depth.note: dynamic topography of the ocean floor: residual depth anomalies of about +-1 km at wavelengths of ~1000 km (Hoggard et al. 2016); zero mean
residual_depth.calibration: rms chosen (E08 run o) so that 6.3 % of the ocean is deeper than 5.5 km, as on Earth (1-degree hypsometry); peaks of about +-0.8 km stay within the observed +-1 km

subgrid_relief.note: expected peak-to-valley relief within a 10 km cell

20.analogue: Tibesti, plume massif on a craton (Emi Koussi 3415 m)

33.analogue: curved island arc around a small sea (Banda arc); arc volcano Stromboli (924 m)
33.note: the island is a ring ~300 km across with a lagoon; the E04 point lies in the lagoon, so the island's own land cells within radius_km take a range profile instead of a cone

canon_peaks.note: point features of E04 drawn as cones; positions from canon_features.geojson

range_noise.note: ridged field 1-|f| breaks envelopes into ridges and valleys

peak_heights_verified: 2026-11-18: every peak_m checked against summit lists and encyclopaedias; see experiments/E08_relief.md
